topic: per-band cancellation penalty of the model used for the live tests

model.note: the exact coefficients loaded on the board during the three-arm live test

definition: penalty_dB = 20log10(|H-Hhat|) - 20log10(|H|); positive means the loop gain with cancellation exceeds the loop gain without it in that bin
calibration: six white-noise segments, 2 s total, coherence-gated at 0.7, n=8192

at_8285_hz.note: 8285 Hz is the frequency the live loop oscillated at

verdict: the model's magnitude is right at 8.4 kHz (9.17 vs 9.14 dB) but its phase is about 33 degrees off, so |H-Hhat| is as large as |H|: cancellation achieves nothing there and slightly raises the loop gain. That band carries the largest |H| of the fixture (about +9 dB), so it is exactly where the usable gain is capped. Below 3 kHz the same model cancels by 10-11 dB.
implication: fixing the 8.4 kHz phase, not the magnitude, is what would let cancel exceed the gain that bypass already tolerates
